title: Gary Fisch raises $380,000 for nonprofits at JBWS Spring Tastings fundraiser
text:
Gary Fisch raises $380,000 for nonprofits at JBWS Spring Tastings fundraiser
Gary Fisch raised $380,000 in seven minutes at an auction for Jersey Battered Women Services (JBWS) Spring Tastings fundraiser in Randolph on Aug. 19, where the only prize was a hug.
Fisch, co-owner of three Gary’s Wine and Marketplace stores in North Jersey and a board member of the New Jersey Business and Industry Association, said, "Giving back is part of who we are. For nearly 40 years, we've believed that being a successful local business comes with a responsibility to invest in the communities that support us." He added, "Our goal is to help strengthen the neighborhoods we serve by partnering with organizations that improve lives, support families, advance education, promote the arts, and provide critical healthcare and community services."
Fisch and his wife Liz participate year-round in fundraising for nonprofits including Atlantic Health Morristown Medical Center, Morris Arts, Interfaith Food Pantry, and Homeless Solutions. Gary’s signature annual event is Gary’s Grand Tastings, which benefits Atlantic Health Morristown Medical Center as well as other charities. Over time this event has raised over $1 million for these causes.
Tickets are available online for the 2026 Gary’s Grand Tastings scheduled for Nov. 2 at Park Avenue Club in Florham Park. Last year’s event raised over $135,000; this year Fisch hopes to surpass that amount. Through partnership with the Foundation for Morristown Medical Center’s Associate Board of Ambassadors, part of this year's proceeds will support expansion of Deskovick Maternity Center at the hospital.
Although his auctioneer skills are not needed during Gary's Grand Tasting silent auction portion—he practices those skills regularly at JBWS events—a tradition began when he offered hugs after an emotional speech from an abuse survivor left attendees tearful: “It was a very tough thing to follow... so I didn’t know what else to do except start hugging people,” Fisch said.
Sometimes bidding starts slowly but often picks up when he promises matching donations with his wife: “He can often entice someone to make a $15,000 or $20,000 donation if he promises that he and his wife will match that amount.” This approach helped raise $380,000 at this year’s JBWS gala auction on May 18—surpassing their previous record.
The New Jersey Business and Industry Association serves as the nation's largest statewide employer association representing private-sector employers throughout New Jersey; it advances competitive excellence among its members by offering advocacy services and facilitating partnerships between businesses and other entities, according to the official website.
